applied.title: {{name}} applied the {{edit}}
applied.description: {{name}} made the change directly, so the agent model never ran and spent no tokens.

routed.title: New question for the agent
routed.description: {{name}} read this as a new question rather than a change to the current chart, so the agent answered it.

clarify.title: {{name}} asked which one you meant
clarify.description: The request fit more than one option about equally, so {{name}} offered the choices instead of guessing. The agent model did not run.

unresolved.title: {{name}} was not confident
unresolved.description: {{name}} looked for a direct chart edit but was not sure enough to apply one, so the agent took over.

instantReply.title: {{name}} answered directly
instantReply.description: This was a small follow-up {{name}} could answer from the chart itself, so the agent model did not run.

unavailable.title: {{name}} did not answer
unavailable.description: {{name}} did not respond in time, so the agent handled the turn as usual.

handedOff.title: {{name}} passed the {{edit}} to the agent
handedOff.description: {{name}} worked out the {{edit}} but it needed more than a direct edit, so the agent finished it.

general.title: Ask AI
general.description: Configure organization-wide AI features, providers, and defaults.
general.aiRouterDescription: Route user questions to the best agent automatically.
general.defaultModelDescription: Choose the model and reasoning default for new AI agent chats. Users can still change it in each chat.
general.highReasoningDescription: Start new chats with high reasoning enabled for the selected model.
general.providersDescription: Your own keys take precedence over the instance keys.
general.reviewTurnsDescription: Process every agent turn to surface semantic layer gaps, project context improvements, and admin recommendations. For connected projects, Lightdash can suggest pull requests that improve context and semantic definitions.
general.reviewsPaused: Paused — your AI provider key can’t run the review model (Claude Haiku). Reviews run on your own key, so they resume when it has access.

surfaces.description: Where agents can be reached. Per-agent access still applies on every surface.
surfaces.lightdashUiDescription: Homepage card, navbar action, and agent chat.
surfaces.dataAppsDescription: AI analysis inside data apps is configured under <anchor>Data apps · AI analysis</anchor>.
surfaces.slackDisconnected: Slack isn't connected. Add the integration in Integrations → Slack first.

dataAppModels.title: Data Apps models
dataAppModels.description: Which models users can pick when building a Data App. Data Apps run the Claude CLI, which picks the latest model in each tier — so these are set separately from Ask AI models. Apps already built with a hidden model keep working.
dataAppModels.lockedTooltip: At least one model must stay available

retention.title: Thread retention
retention.description: Automatically delete agent threads after a period of inactivity. Agents can shorten this window but not extend it.
retention.confirmBody: Threads inactive for longer than {{window}} will be permanently deleted across all agents in this organization, starting within the hour. This cannot be undone.

reviewNotifications.slackDescription: Post to a Slack channel when a review run surfaces findings that need review. Assignment notifications are always sent as a direct message and in the in-app bell.
reviewNotifications.slackAria: Post AI review findings to Slack

routing.confirmLeave: You have unsaved routing instructions. Are you sure you want to leave without saving?
routing.confirmSwitch: You have unsaved routing instructions. Are you sure you want to switch projects without saving?
routing.title: Routing instructions
routing.description: Tell the router how to direct questions for a project. For example, send billing questions to a specific agent. Type @ to tag an agent. Rules guide the router but never override an agent's access restrictions.
routing.tooFewAgents: This project has fewer than two accessible agents, so the router won't run here yet. You can still prepare instructions.
routing.placeholder: e.g. Route billing and invoicing questions to @Finance Agent. Type @ to tag an agent.

providers.gatewayDescription: Optional. Send requests for this key to a proxy or gateway that speaks this provider's API. Model names are passed through unchanged.
providers.gatewayError: Enter an http(s) URL without credentials, query parameters or a fragment
providers.lockedNote: Disabled while your organization uses another provider key — {{label}} models can't be selected, so AI agents never fall back to the instance's {{label}} key. Add your own {{label}} API key to make these models available.
providers.instanceKeyNote: AI agents using {{label}} models currently run on the instance's default key. Add your organization's {{label}} key — or turn off availability above — to keep all AI agent usage on your own keys.
providers.title: AI providers & models
providers.description: Use your organization's own Anthropic, Google Gemini, or OpenAI API key for AI features, and control which models users can pick. Keys are stored encrypted and never shown again after saving; when set, they take precedence over the instance-level keys. Agents already using a hidden model keep working — it just can't be selected again.
providers.orgKeysTitle_one: AI agents run on your organization's API key
providers.orgKeysTitle_other: AI agents run on your organization's API keys
providers.orgKeysBody_one: Agent responses and background agent tasks (thread titles, suggestions, summaries) use the key configured below — never the instance's default keys.
providers.orgKeysBody_other: Agent responses and background agent tasks (thread titles, suggestions, summaries) use the keys configured below — never the instance's default keys.
providers.autopilotNote: Autopilot setup shows which provider, model, and key it uses. Scheduled runs can make multiple model calls and incur usage on that key.

bedrock.title: Amazon Bedrock credentials
bedrock.description: Each credential pins Ask AI to one AWS region. Projects can select a credential; anything without a project — Slack routing, thread titles — uses the default.
bedrock.unreadable: {{count}} credential(s) cannot be read with the current encryption secret. AI requests pinned to them fail rather than falling back to another region, so replace each one with a complete configuration.
bedrock.onlyProviderNote: While Bedrock is configured it is the only provider Ask AI uses, so agents pinned to another provider stop working until you repoint them. Verified-answer semantic search and AI repository editing are unavailable, because both would send content outside these regions.

geographyNotes.jp: Requests stay in Japan (Tokyo and Osaka inference profiles).
geographyNotes.us: Requests may be served by any US region.
geographyNotes.eu: Requests may be served by any European region.
geographyNotes.apac: Requests may be served by any Asia-Pacific region, across countries.
geographyNotes.global: Requests may be served by any supported region worldwide.

bedrockModal.replaceNote: The stored configuration cannot be read, so every field must be re-entered.
bedrockModal.intro: Use a Bedrock API key, not an AWS access key pair. The region you pick decides where inference runs, so enable these models in that region of your AWS account.
bedrockModal.name: Name
bedrockModal.nameDescription: How projects refer to this credential.
bedrockModal.geographyDescription: Where Amazon Bedrock may process requests — the region above only receives them.
bedrockModal.keepKey: Leave blank to keep the saved key.

linear.clientIdPlaceholder: Paste the client ID from Linear
linear.title: Linear issues
linear.connectedDescription: New findings create a Linear issue automatically. Existing open findings can be exported below. Each issue links both ways; status is not synced.
linear.disconnectedDescription: Send review findings to Linear as issues. Each issue links both ways. Status is not synced.
linear.toggleAria: Create Linear issues for AI review findings
linear.step1Description: Opens Linear with the callback already filled in. Private app, no client secret.
linear.step2Title: Paste the client ID and connect
linear.step2Description: Use the public client ID from the app you just created.
linear.reconnectTitle: Reconnect Linear to keep exporting issues
linear.reconnectDescription: The saved app can no longer create issues. Create a new private app or reconnect with the same client ID.
linear.allProjectsDescription: Findings from every project, including ones created later.
linear.projectDescription: Optional. Issues without a project still go to the selected team.

jira.title: Jira issues
jira.description: Send review findings to Jira automatically. Existing open findings can be exported below; status is not synced.
jira.toggleAria: Create Jira issues for AI review findings
jira.step1Description: In the developer console create an OAuth 2.0 integration. Under Permissions add the Jira API and tick the classic scopes read:jira-work and write:jira-work. Under Authorization set this callback URL.
jira.step2Title: Paste the client ID and secret
jira.step2Description: Both are on the app's Settings page. The secret is stored encrypted and only used for this organization. Connecting opens Atlassian: sign in there with an account that has Jira on the site you want to use, or Atlassian shows Access denied.
jira.siteDescription: Choose the site that will receive review issues.
jira.allProjectsDescription: Findings from every Lightdash project, including ones created later.

maxSteps.label: Maximum steps
maxSteps.description: The maximum number of model steps the coordinator may take in a deep research run.

maxToolCalls.label: Maximum tool calls
maxToolCalls.description: The maximum number of tool calls across a deep research run.

maxWarehouseQueries.label: Maximum warehouse queries
maxWarehouseQueries.description: The maximum number of warehouse queries across a deep research run.

maxTokens.label: Maximum tokens
maxTokens.description: The maximum total model tokens consumed across a deep research run.

deadlineMinutes.label: Time limit (minutes)
deadlineMinutes.description: The wall-clock limit for a deep research run before it stops and reports what it has.

deepResearch.runLimitsDescription: Ceilings applied to every deep research run in your organization. A run that reaches any of these limits stops and reports what it has.
deepResearch.rawSqlDescription: Let Deep Research run raw SQL when the initiating user has SQL Runner permission. Disable to keep investigations on governed explores and metrics.
deepResearch.title: Deep research
deepResearch.description: Configure organization-wide data access and safety limits for deep research runs.

mcpGeneral.title: General
mcpGeneral.description: Configure how MCP (Model Context Protocol) clients access Lightdash agents and content.
mcpGeneral.enableAgentsDescription: Make agent tools and context available to MCP clients. Per-agent access still applies.
mcpGeneral.allowWritesDescription: Let MCP clients create and edit charts and dashboards in this organization. Disable to prevent unintended changes to managed content; reading content over MCP stays available either way, and individual users are still bound by their existing permissions.

claudeDesktop.s1: In Claude Desktop, open Customize → Connectors and choose Add custom connector.
claudeDesktop.s2: Name it Lightdash and paste this server URL. Remote connectors need a publicly reachable HTTPS URL.
claudeDesktop.s3: Add the connector, then sign in to Lightdash and approve access.

claudeCode.s1: Run this command in your terminal.
claudeCode.s2: In Claude Code, run /mcp, select Lightdash, then choose Authenticate.

codex.s1: Add the server and start sign-in from your terminal.
codex.s3: Start a new Codex session to use the Lightdash tools.

cursor.s1: Add this server to your project’s .cursor/mcp.json.
cursor.s2: Open Cursor Settings → MCP & Integrations and connect Lightdash.

vscode.s1: Add this server to your project’s .vscode/mcp.json.
vscode.s2: Run MCP: List Servers from the Command Palette, select Lightdash, and start it.
vscode.s3: Sign in to Lightdash when prompted, then use the tools in Copilot agent mode.

other.s1: Add a remote MCP server and choose Streamable HTTP as the transport.
other.s2: Name it Lightdash and paste this server URL.
other.s3: Choose OAuth authentication, sign in to Lightdash, and approve access.

steps.signInBrowser: Sign in to Lightdash in your browser and approve access.

projectRegion.noCredentials: No AI provider credentials are configured for this organization yet. An organization admin can add them in Organization settings → Ask AI.

projectRegion.description: Where this project's Ask AI requests are processed.
